image_description: A close-up, low-angle photograph of a large Triceratops skull fossil mounted on display stands in front of a stone building facade. The skull features the characteristic three horns (two long brow horns, one short nasal horn) and a massive solid bony frill. The texture is rough, fossilized bone with visible cracks and weathering. No body, limbs, or tail are visible; only the head structure is present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Three prominent horns: two long brow horns projecting forward and upward above the eyes, and a shorter nasal horn on the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the iconic triceratops horn configuration: two large supraorbital horns curving forward/upward and a smaller nasal horn. They are structurally sound and correctly positioned relative to the eye sockets.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Beak is parrot-like with a sharp, keratinous cutting edge.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rostral bone (beak core) is visible at the front of the skull, exhibiting the curved, hooked shape typical of ceratopsian beaks. While the keratin sheath is missing (as it is a fossil), the underlying bony structure matches the 'parrot-like' description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is quadrupedal with columnar, elephant-like limbs.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop of the skull only. The body and limbs are completely outside the frame and not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bony frill (neck shield) extending posteriorly from the skull, with width dramatically exceeding the skull itself.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill is prominently displayed behind the skull. It is wide, solid, and extends significantly beyond the width of the facial portion of the skull, matching the morphological description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Frill is solid bone with a smooth outer surface and possible epoccipital (marginal) bumps.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The frill appears as a solid plate of bone. The edges show irregularities consistent with epoccipitals or fossil damage/weathering. The surface texture is consistent with fossilized bone.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is inferred to have been covered in large, hexagonal scales with possible quill-like structures along the back and tail.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a bare fossil skull. There is no skin, scales, or soft tissue preserved or depicted in the image.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Forelimbs are shorter than hindlimbs creating a sloping backline.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are not visible in the image.
The tail is not visible in the image.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The texture of the fossil is highly detailed but exhibits a slight 'digital noise' or uniform granularity that could suggest AI generation or heavy post-processing, though it closely mimics real porous bone. No structural melting or fusion observed.

The lines of the building facade in the background show slight warping/inconsistency in perspective convergence, particularly around the window frames on the right. This is a common subtle artifact in AI-generated scenes involving architecture.
